cards.d: An administrator is a person who controls a business, company, or organization.
cards.e: Everyone in the store did whatever the administrator asked them to do.

cards.d: If someone is affluent, they are wealthy.
cards.e: People in the city are usually more affluent than people in the country.

cards.d: To audit means to inspect financial records from a person or business.
cards.e: The government usually audits companies that report lower than usual incomes.

cards.d: To automate a company means to install machines or computers to do the work.
cards.e: When the bank automated, it started installing ATM machines.

cards.d: To bribe someone means to illegally persuade them for a favor with money.
cards.e: The judge was bribed so that she would set the suspect free.

cards.d: If someone is corrupt, they break the law for money or fame.
cards.e: The corrupt policemen didn’t arrest the man because he gave them money.

cards.d: To dispose of something means to get rid of it.
cards.e: He disposed of the can by throwing it into the recycle bin.

cards.d: A headquarters is a building where the bosses of a company work.
cards.e: He drove the long route to headquarters because it was a nice day.

cards.d: An incentive is what makes a person want to do something.
cards.e: The chance of winning a prize was incentive to get people to play the game.

cards.d: An infrastructure is a collection of services needed to run a society or business.
cards.e: Power lines are important parts of a city’s infrastructure.

cards.d: To legislate means to make laws.
cards.e: Senators have to legislate fairly, so most people will enjoy the benefits.

cards.d: If something is legitimate, then it is acceptable according to the law.
cards.e: She found a legitimate plan to raise extra funds for her vacation.

cards.d: To manipulate something means to skillfully or unfairly control or affect it.
cards.e: The Dr. manipulated the data to make it look like the cure was working.

cards.d: Merchandise is goods ready to be purchased or sold.
cards.e: The store added more merchandise because there were more shoppers.

cards.d: Retail is the activity of selling goods to the public, often for personal use.
cards.e: Though cheap to make, once a t-shirt reaches retail, it costs ten times as much.

cards.d: Revenue is the income made by a company.
cards.e: The new products really increased the business’s monthly revenue.

cards.d: Rubbish is trash or waste.
cards.e: The floor around the garbage can was covered with all kinds of rubbish.

cards.d: A subsidy is money given by the government to companies to assist them.
cards.e: The official gave the company a subsidy, so it could open two new factories.

cards.d: A transaction is an act of buying or selling something.
cards.e: Because the clerk was new at the job, the simple transaction took a long time.

cards.d: To violate a law, rule, or agreement means to break it.
cards.e: I was given a ticket because the policeman said I violated the speed limit.
